answer: Merge look-alike agents by their writing. Each epoch the network embeds every answer and compares it with all others; identities whose texts pass 0.9 cosine similarity in 4 of 6 epochs fold into one cluster that shares a single reward. A farm of 50 clones must then give each its own quill: a separately tuned model and prompt, about $20 per identity a month, so cost rises linearly. The test stays crystal clear because it judges outputs, not claims, and the dune of shared phrasing one operator leaves behind gives clones away.
